title: All the key moments from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix
excerpt:
Azerbaijan marked 10 years on the F1 calendar with another action-packed weekend of competition – one that saw George Russell emerge victorious and cut team mate Kimi Antonelli’s advantage at the top of the championship.

Elsewhere, Isack Hadjar marked his return from injury with a fine podium finish, several drivers got caught up in Safety Car restart drama, and the race for the F2 title stepped up a gear.

Read on for a recap of all the key moments from the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix…

Russell claims victory despite Verstappen’s late challenge

For a large portion of Saturday’s race on the streets of Baku, Russell dominated proceedings as he had done a day earlier in Qualifying, where he grabbed pole position by a whopping eight tenths.

Having held the lead at the start, the Briton gradually increased his lead over the chasing pack, initially led by Oscar Piastri, and his margin stood at more than 10 seconds when the Safety Car was deployed on Lap 31 after Alex Albon found the barrier.

Russell then nailed a tricky restart, with the long main straight and late start/finish line offering those behind the chance to use the slipstream for an overtake, which Max Verstappen did successfully on Piastri.

It set up a titanic final leg as the pair circulated together and never drifted more than one second apart, their pace and brushes with the walls meaning they left the rest of the field behind.

Russell managed the gap enough to prevent Verstappen from having a run down the main straight, but a yellow flag on the final lap for Valtteri Bottas’s stricken car at Turn 15 meant he backed off and lost crucial power from his turbo.

It almost opened the door for Verstappen, who fell short of victory by just one tenth as Russell took his first F1 grand slam and just his third win of the season.

It couldn’t have come at a better time, with Russell cutting the gap to team mate Antonelli in the drivers’ standings to 66 points and, perhaps more importantly, having found race-winning performance from his car for the first time since June.

Double Red Bull podium after a stellar Hadjar comeback

Verstappen was left frustrated after Qualifying in Baku, as the Red Bull driver went from looking like a pole position threat to being left P8 on the grid after several issues.

The Dutchman certainly wasn’t lacking pace in the race though, making short work of those ahead until he got stuck behind Piastri in the early stages, only overtaking the McLaren man after a Safety Car restart.

Verstappen then pushed Russell hard for victory, which included glancing the wall on the entry to Turn 16 several times before ultimately falling short of his first win in 2026.

Hadjar hails 'first proper podium' with P3 in Baku

Despite failing to reach the top step, Red Bull enjoyed their best weekend of the season so far as Hadjar completed the rostrum in third to cap off a remarkable return to F1.

The Frenchman had missed the last three race weekends with a wrist injury sustained during the summer break, but immediately hit his stride as he qualified fourth.

After allowing Verstappen through in the early laps, Hadjar shadowed his team mate and eventually overtook Piastri – as the Australian made a mistake at Turn 1 – for just his second podium of the season.

Safety Car chaos shakes up the race

Just as it looked like Russell would go entirely unchallenged on his way to victory, Albon locked up and drove straight into the barrier at Turn 6, starting a chain of events that would throw the race into chaos.

With the Safety Car deployed and the field neutralised, the majority dived into the pits and returned to the track as they were – it wasn’t until the restart that things fell apart for Alpine, McLaren and Racing Bulls.

Russell shakily led from a charging Verstappen whilst further back, Franco Colapinto became one of the many drivers to fall victim to a lock-up as he failed to make Turn 1, colliding with his team mate Pierre Gasly.

The Frenchman was squeezed into Lando Norris as a result, sending the trio onto the run-off area with damage that saw them all retire from the race. Almost simultaneously, Racing Bulls’ Arvid Lindblad tagged the rear of Liam Lawson’s car, prompting the latter’s sarcastic comment: “I love getting taken out by my team mate. That’s pretty sick.”

Once the action resumed for a second time, the second McLaren of Piastri watched a potential podium slip out of his hands as he was also caught out at the first corner, locking up and going wide before he rejoined the track in P15.

The disorder was detrimental for some, but it played perfectly into Antonelli’s hands as he improved to P5, with Haas and Williams also making the most of it to score some rare points.

A point-less weekend for McLaren

The Norris of two weeks ago was devastated to miss out on the win in Madrid, but even he couldn’t have predicted how much worse McLaren’s weekend in Azerbaijan would be as they left the round with zero points.

It was pretty clear that the low-speed corners of Baku wouldn’t play to the team’s strengths, so Piastri taking P3 in Qualifying was a pleasant surprise – and with Norris lining up P5, a decent points haul was on the table.

However, while the Aussie spent most of the race fiercely defending his place in the top three, his team mate could find no solution to his lack of pace, especially down the long straights. He temporarily got ahead of Red Bull’s Hadjar at the start before the Frenchman fought back, with Verstappen similarly overtaking him shortly afterwards.

'Some drivers shouldn't be in F1' - Norris on Baku clash

Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton was the next to get past after Norris made one of a handful of errors, his most consequential being a lock-up that allowed Gasly and Antonelli to demote him further down the running order.

But it was a mistake from Colapinto, rather than Norris, that brought his day to an early end as he was taken out by the clash between the Alpine drivers, causing his later statement that there are “some drivers that shouldn’t be in F1”.

As mentioned above, Piastri didn’t have a good time of it either as he similarly lost control at Turn 1, leaving him unable to do anything as his competitors powered past. He gained a position from Bottas’ late crash, but finishing P14 instead of P15 didn’t really soften the blow.

Baku’s 10th anniversary is one to remember

This year’s Azerbaijan Grand Prix marked 10 years since Baku arrived on the calendar back in 2016. It has proven a popular addition with fans and drivers alike, delivering plenty of memorable moments across the years.

One thing Baku often throws up is intra-team clashes, with Daniel Ricciardo and Verstappen’s crash in 2018 living long in the memory, while Esteban Ocon and Sergio Perez collided back in 2017 when both at Force India.

As such, it was fitting that the 2026 edition saw not one but two intra-team moments, the biggest of which involved Colapinto and Gasly’s Alpines, which led to both retiring from the race. Racing Bulls pair Lawson and Lindblad also made contact, but both were able to continue.

Lawson baffled by Lindblad clash that 'sucks' in Baku

Baku was also the venue where Piastri’s championship hopes began to unravel last season, making it somewhat fitting that the current leader in the standings almost suffered a similar fate this year – Antonelli crashing in Qualifying, but unlike the Australian, able to recover to fifth and salvage some points.

Those are not the only things 2026 will be remembered for, with Russell’s emphatic pole position, his narrow margin of victory over a resurgent Verstappen, McLaren’s disastrous lock-ups and a drag race over the line for seventh place also worth noting.

All in all, the 2026 edition delivered on drama and wheel-to-wheel action, and has even sparked life back into the championship battle at Mercedes.

F2 championship hots up

Going into Baku, Nikola Tsolov had a seven-point lead over Rafael Camara in the F2 standings, but that all changed following not one, but two Feature Races in the City of Winds.

Tsolov did not finish the first Feature Race after being involved in a multi-car incident, which was won by Alexander Dunne from pole. Martinius Stenshorne took second to give Rodin Motorsport a 1-2, with Dino Beganovic third for DAMS Lucas Oil.

With Camara finishing fourth, Tsolov’s lead in the standings was gone, and he finished behind his rival in the second Feature Race too, with Camara taking a seven-point lead overall following his victory.

Camara was fortunate to get the win, having finished second on the road – but Dunne was penalised for crossing the white line on pit entry, which dropped him from first to third.

Dunne is only 18 points behind in the championship now, so he cannot be discounted in terms of the title, with racing set to resume in Qatar later this season.

title: Azerbaijan mistake 'certainly took me by surprise' – Piastri
excerpt:
Oscar Piastri admits that the lock-up which potentially cost the Australian driver a podium in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix "certainly took me by surprise", on a day where McLaren failed to score a point.

Piastri had enjoyed a strong first half to the 51-lap race around Baku's historic streets, overtaking Charles Leclerc for second through the opening corner.

The McLaren driver then held off the charging Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar as both Red Bull drivers showed strong pace early on.

Piastri maintained second when pitting under the first of two Safety Cars, but at the restart, he was unable to hold Verstappen behind and dropped to third.

A second Safety Car was called after a collision at the opening corner, involving McLaren team mate Lando Norris, and Piastri once again faced pressure from behind at the restart, this time from Hadjar.

Having initially rebuffed the Frenchman, Piastri went defensive into Turn 1 on the following lap, suffering a double lock-up that sent him into the run-off area and down the order.

‘Some drivers shouldn’t be in F1’ – Norris on Baku clash

"Just disappointed. Obviously I think the first stint and the first half of the race was very encouraging and then from there on, it kind of unravelled," said Piastri, who was eventually classified in P14.

"The lock-up I need to understand what happened because it certainly took me by surprise. I need to go and have a look, but obviously very disappointing not to have a result at the end."

Piastri has endured a difficult season so far in 2026, taking just two podiums with the last one coming at Miami in May, while Norris has taken two wins from the previous five races.

Despite missing out on the result, Piastri was encouraged by his performance over the weekend in Baku having been back towards the front of the field.

"I think once the dust settles there will be a lot of positives from this weekend," he said.

"I think Qualifying yesterday was good, I think in general I felt much more comfortable, well maybe not more comfortable but I've had more direction on what I need to do with the car.

"There's plenty of positives it just hurts obviously when you don't have any points or a trophy at the end."

title: Bortoleto handed penalty after yellow flag infringement
excerpt:
Gabriel Bortoleto has been handed a time penalty after the Audi driver was judged to have overtaken under a yellow flag.

The Brazilian finished P13 during Saturday's 51-lap race around the streets of Baku on a weekend where Audi struggled to challenge for the points, as team mate Nico Hulkenberg finished in P11.

Post-race, the stewards summoned Bortoleto for an incident which took place between Turns 6 and 7 during the first lap after the first Safety Car restart.

The stewards noted that "marshal posts in this area were displaying physical “SC” boards together with waved Yellow Flags", following a crash between Alpine team mates Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto, as well as Lando Norris' McLaren, at Turn 1.

The document noted that although Bortoleto initially reacted to the yellow flags, "he did not see any corresponding electronic indication and did not receive a Safety Car indication on his steering wheel", and that "he was also informed by his Team that the Safety Car had not been deployed".

As a result, Bortoleto proceeded to overtake Sergio Perez's Cadillac prior to the appearance of the Safety Car, with stewards determining that "as the Safety Car had not been deployed, Bortoleto cannot be considered to have overtaken another car under Safety Car conditions".

They did however find that Bortoleto still made an overtake while a yellow flag was present, handing him a 10-second penalty which dropped him down to P15 and last of the classified runners.

The document continued: "A waved Yellow Flag is an instruction in its own right and must be respected irrespective of any accompanying signal.

"A driver cannot disregard a Yellow Flag based on his own assessment as to why it has been displayed or whether it should have been displayed."

title: What the teams said – Race day in Azerbaijan
excerpt:
Mercedes

George Russell led from pole and built a commanding lead in the first segment of the race. He was cruising to the win until two Safety Cars neutralised his advantage. With a rapid Verstappen suddenly on his heels, Russell had to work hard in the final few laps to hold on to the win – even clipping the wall in his Mercedes at one stage. But despite losing his Boost on the very last lap, he just about held on for his first Grand Prix win since Austria.

As for Kimi Antonelli, he did not make the sort of progress many expected, initially going backwards at the start. Slowly but surely he did climb into the top 10, and then was very fortunate to avoid the crash at the first restart that happened on his outside. The Italian limited his losses with a move on Lewis Hamilton, but ran out of time to catch up and pass Charles Leclerc. Fifth was still a very decent recovery – aided by the Safety Cars closing the pack back up.

George Russell, 1st

"It's been an incredible weekend and probably one of the strongest of my career so far. I really enjoyed that race and that final stint was some of the most fun I’ve had in a Formula One race. We had strong pace throughout and were able to build a good gap, so when the Safety Car came out it was a little frustrating, but around a circuit like Baku that's always a possibility.

"The restart was probably the most stressful moment of the afternoon with Max right behind me, but I managed it well and from there it was all about staying focused and not making any mistakes. In the final stint we were both pushing hard, and whilst it was intense in the car, those are the moments you enjoy as a driver.

"I've felt comfortable all weekend, and at the moment things seem to be coming naturally behind the wheel. We're in a good place, but Formula One changes very quickly so you have to keep pushing. The aim is to keep working hard, keep building this momentum and hopefully continue fighting at the front over the races ahead."

Kimi Antonelli, 5th

"Today was about damage limitation. I took no unnecessary risks at all and focused on maximising the points scored for the team. It was difficult to make progress at times because we were in an overtaking train, but I focused on staying out of trouble and taking the opportunities when they came.

"It was one of those weekends where everything doesn't quite go your way. The pace wasn't quite there for me today, but given where we started, I have to be happy with P5. I just tried to race the race in front of me, stay patient and bring the car home. We were able to benefit from some of the opportunities that came our way and score as many points as possible.

"Luckily, we have another race coming up very soon, so I'm fully focused on that and really looking forward to it."

Bradley Lord, Deputy Team Principal

"It's been a really impressive weekend from George, he simply hasn’t put a foot wrong. He hit the ground running in FP1 and set the pace from then on. Even with the way the Safety Cars and restarts unfolded, he managed everything that was thrown at him and delivered a race that was completely error free, even with Verstappen breathing down his neck in the final stint. Around Baku, that's easier said than done.

"Today's race was always going to be a different challenge for Kimi. With the limited running he had through the weekend, it was important that he didn't come into the race thinking it was Monza Part Two and trying to force the issue. Instead, he drove the race that was in front of him, showed a really good grasp of the bigger picture, and recovered well to P5. That was an impressive performance in its own right.

"It's a great way for the team to start this demanding triple-header. We've scored strongly with both cars, executed well throughout the weekend, and given ourselves a solid foundation heading into the next race. Malaysia is a special event for us given our title partnership with PETRONAS, and we'll take the learnings from this weekend, keep working hard, and look to maximise our performance again next week."

Andrew Shovlin, Trackside Engineering Director

"Congratulations to George and the team on a fantastic victory. He has been quick throughout the weekend and converted a brilliant pole position into an assured race win today. The Safety Cars kept things interesting and there was pressure at each restart, but George managed the race superbly and delivered when it mattered most.

"Kimi also did an excellent job to recover from P16 on the grid to finish fifth. After yesterday's disappointment, he stayed focused and made the most of the opportunities that came his way. His pace was strong throughout the race and he worked his way through the field with several decisive overtakes.

"The Safety Cars meant there was little opportunity to relax at any stage of the race, particularly for George at the front, but both drivers handled the challenges well and extracted the maximum from the opportunities available to them.

"We've had a competitive car from the first laps in Baku and it's pleasing to have converted that pace into a strong result. George was in control throughout the race, while Kimi's recovery drive demonstrated both the pace of the car and his determination after a difficult qualifying session. We leave Azerbaijan with good momentum and plenty of positives to take into the next event."

title: Colapinto gets 5-place grid drop for Bahrain GP in Malaysia
excerpt:
Franco Colapinto has been given a five-place grid penalty for next weekend’s Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia after causing a multi-car incident at the Baku City Circuit on Saturday.

Colapinto was attempting to make up ground during the first Safety Car restart on Lap 36/51 when he went too deep at Turn 1, taking out both Alpine team mate Pierre Gasly and the McLaren of Lando Norris.

After reviewing the footage and data available to them, the stewards determined that Colapinto “was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision”, and thus handed out a penalty.

Given that Colapinto also retired from the race, a 10-second time penalty will instead be converted into a drop of five grid positions at the Sepang International Circuit.

“Following the restart, COL approached GAS from behind into Turn 1,” read the stewards’ decision document. “COL braked too late and entered the corner on the inside at a speed which did not allow him to make the corner in a controlled manner. He overshot the corner and made contact with the left-hand side of GAS, who then hit NOR and both cars retired.

“The stewards considered that COL was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision. Although the incident occurred at the first corner following the restart, there was no contribution from another driver which would justify applying the first-lap/first corner more linient approach.

“The standard penalty for causing a collision is a 10-second time penalty. As COL had retired from the race and was therefore unable to serve the time penalty, the stewards converted the penalty to a drop of five grid positions at the next race in which the driver participates, in accordance which Article B1.9.6.(e) of the FIA FIA 2026 F1 Regulations.”

Speaking to the media following the incident, and before the stewards dished out their penalty, Colapinto offered apologies to Gasly, Norris and his Alpine team.

“Just [a] bit of disappointment, for myself, for the team,” he said. “Just a big sorry to all of them, to the factory, to Pierre of course. [I] took him out, so [I’m] really disappointed. We were both in a position to score points, [it] was a big day for the team and [I] did a big mistake. A big sorry, it shouldn’t happen.”

Giving his verdict, Gasly added: “I don’t think I really have words and I don’t need the words now. We’ll manage it together as a team. I’m obviously very disappointed for all the guys, P7 and P10 was a very good race, good pace. Honestly, I have no idea how to answer your question. [We’ve] got to move on.”

Norris, meanwhile, summed up: “I just got taken out… just some drivers that shouldn’t be in F1, to be honest.”

title: Hadjar hails ‘first proper podium’ with P3 in Baku
excerpt:
Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar was all smiles after completing his comeback from a “very long six weeks” on the sidelines with a podium finish at the Baku City Circuit.

Hadjar missed events at Zandvoort, Monza and the all-new Madring track over the last month, having injured his wrist while training in the summer break.

However, the Frenchman got the green light to compete again in Azerbaijan, where he gradually built his speed throughout practice before qualifying fourth and racing his way to third place.

It marked Hadjar’s third podium in F1, but the first that he feels was earned “on pure pace”, given that he gained from Lando Norris’ retirement at the 2025 Dutch Grand Prix, while representing Racing Bulls, and from Pierre Gasly’s penalties in Monaco earlier this year.

Sharing his thoughts post-race, Hadjar beamed: “I’m happy. It’s been a very long six weeks. It’s been like six weeks since I enjoyed myself.

“I think it was the right time to come back. I felt strong. This weekend I really took it step by step. It’s a track where you can end up in the wall really quickly, and I didn’t need that, to gain the confidence. It was a very slow build-up, but it brought me here.

“I’m very, very happy for an actual first proper podium on pure pace. I’m very, very delighted.”

Hadjar was further boosted by his recovering wrist holding up well across 51 laps of racing on Saturday afternoon – as a busy final phase of the 2026 season looms.

“I’m completely satisfied,” he said. “Even though it’s a bit numb, I’m happy. I’m really looking forward to getting racing [again]. It’s going to be a very packed schedule. I can’t wait to be in Sepang.”

title: Lawson baffled by Lindblad clash in Baku that ‘sucks’
excerpt:
Liam Lawson admitted that he didn’t understand what team mate Arvid Lindblad was hoping to achieve in a move that saw the Racing Bulls pair make contact in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, with the New Zealander summarising that “it sucks for our race”.

After both drivers recovered from being knocked out in Q2, they found themselves in contention for a double points finish heading into the final part of the race, having capitalised on a Safety Car to pit for fresh tyres.

Coming from behind, Lindblad took the inside line at Turn 1 on the restart and tagged the rear of Lawson’s car, sending him into a spin on the run-off area. Lawson dropped down the order as a result and finished P12 upon his return to the team.

Asked for his view on the incident, he said: “I need to watch it. We were all coming into Turn 1 on the restart and I just got smoked from my left. It put a hole in my floor as well.

“I don’t really know what gap he was looking for in the middle of both of us going into Turn 1 – I just don’t understand it. Obviously great points for the team but it sucks for our race.”

Lindblad, meanwhile, believed that he had nowhere else to go, as he explained: “At the back where we were, we’d gone about three times on the straight before we actually went because the field wasn’t bunched up well at all.

“It was just an absolute mess going into Turn 1. Everyone was moving a lot. Obviously a bit of a shame to hit Liam but if you see the incident, you can see there's not much I could’ve done. I came and immediately apologised to him, and obviously I apologised to the team because there could’ve been two of us up there today.”

The 19-year-old was able to continue in the top 10 and ultimately placed P7 after passing Haas’ Esteban Ocon over the line, with a miniscule 0.030s separating the pair.

It marked an important result in the midfield battle against Alpine, especially as Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto retired from the race in Baku following a more detrimental intra-team collision that happened at almost the same time as the one for Racing Bulls.

“On the bright side, let’s take the points,” Lindblad said. “It’s been a very difficult weekend – we struggled to get out of Q1, to be honest. To be here now scoring good points whilst our competitors are out is obviously amazing considering the struggles, so I’m very happy.

“Obviously we had some fortune on our side. The pace is important but it’s the points that matter in the end. We scored the points today.

“The main focus is to understand why we have struggled this week, why we haven’t been faster, but of course we’re absolutely over the moon to score solid points on a weekend that we aren’t fast. It’s always about damage limitation when you’re struggling on a weekend. There’s nothing more we could’ve done today, so it was great.”

Despite the unfortunate conclusion to his race, Lawson agreed with his team mate, adding: “We got very lucky today – they were much quicker than us and they have been all weekend. We need to try and turn it around next week.”

title: Verstappen 'was trying everything' in quest for Baku victory
excerpt:
Max Verstappen admits he "was trying everything" to claim victory on the streets of Baku, the Red Bull driver eventually falling short by just one tenth against George Russell.

The Dutchman was left a frustrated eighth on the grid for Saturday's 51-lap race after issues in Qualifying, but Verstappen quickly began to make progress with the medium tyre.

Moving into third, Verstappen demoted Oscar Piastri's McLaren for second at the first of two Safety car restarts, allowing him to challenge race leader Russell in the closing stages.

"Starting in P8 I knew it wasn't going to be that straightforward but we worked our way quite nicely up into the top three but that first stint was very tricky," said the four-time World Champion.

"That medium tyre was just not very good, not having the grip that I think the soft tyres had so was just trying to survive on that stint to try and stay with the guys on the soft.

"I think that Safety Car came at the right time for everyone to box onto that soft, because once we were on that soft tyre, it felt a lot better, just miles faster.

"I think that also showed once George and I were on the soft, we were pulling away quite a lot over everyone else."

Verstappen stayed on the cusp of a one second gap to Russell over the final laps down the main straight, with Red Bull enjoying straight-line speed during the race.

A yellow flag at Turn 15 after Valtteri Bottas crashed gifted Verstappen the chance to gain an even stronger slipstream on the run to the line for the final time. But the Dutchman ultimately fell short by just one tenth, meaning he has still yet to record a victory during the 2026 season.

"I was trying everything that I have available," said Verstappen in his quest to pass Russell, which included glancing the wall on the entry to Turn 16 several times.

"Of course on the last lap because there was a yellow, I think George picked up a bit of boost lag, so he didn't pull out of Turn 15 and that gave me a little bit more of an opportunity and that's why it was so close to the line. We were constantly one second, so we were very close to each other."

title: Antonelli vows to learn from ‘worst weekend of the season’
excerpt:
Kimi Antonelli made clear that the Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend “taught me a lot” after enduring his “worst weekend of the season” on Baku’s streets.

Antonelli’s start to the weekend was hampered by technical problems in practice before he dramatically crashed out in the opening phase of Qualifying – leaving him down in 16th on the grid, with team mate George Russell on pole.

While Antonelli recovered to fifth position on race day, Russell’s pole-to-victory drive means the Italian’s championship lead has been cut from 81 points to 66.

Reflecting on his race, and the event as a whole, Antonelli said: “I think it’s one of those days where you have to be happy with P5. Obviously it was the worst weekend, by far, of the season.

“I was just… I felt always a step behind, and especially with the mistake in Qualifying, the confidence level was not high. In today’s race I just tried to… today was about damage limitation.

“I didn’t have strong pace, and also after [contact with Haas’ Ollie Bearman at] the Safety Car restart I was carrying big damage, big floor damage.

“It was not easy out there, but I just did my best.”

F1 will move on to Malaysia and Singapore over the next two weekends, as the season heads into a busy final phase – and Antonelli is hopeful that Azerbaijan will turn out to be only a blip in the road.

“I think this weekend taught me a lot,” he said. “I think in many occasions this weekend… I don’t know, probably also with the mindset I was not in the best pace.

“I’ll just make sure that next weekend we get back at the right level.”

title: Arvid Lindblad launches staunch defence after Liam Lawson collision
excerpt:
Arvid Lindblad has insisted his coming together with team-mate Liam Lawson at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix was not intentional.

At a safety car restart on lap 37 of the race in Baku, chaos unfolded at the opening corners as two separate incidents occurred.

One of those involved Lindblad and Lawson, with the latter sent into a spin by his team-mate and demoted down the field.

The stewards opted to take no further action after reviewing the collision, as Lindblad explained that he was caught out by an unexpected change of direction from Esteban Ocon.

"I said I'm sorry on the radio, in the end, it's not intentional," Lindblad told media including RacingNews365.

"If you watch the video back, you can see there's nothing intentional about what I do.

"The stewards said no further action, which obviously I'm happy about.

"In the end, I don't know what you want me to do. We're all on the limit, we all brake very late, and the guy in front of me moves in the last second...

"That's racing, you saw it happen, there were many incidents, so there was nothing I could do."

Lindblad expecting to be 'told off' by Racing Bulls

Lindblad went on to score seventh place at the chequered flag after making two late-race overtakes on the Haas drivers.

This included coming out on top in a drag race to the line with Ocon, crossing the line 0.030s ahead of the Haas driver.

Despite the strong result, Lindblad is expecting that he will get some form of a slap on the wrist from his team.

"They saw that I immediately apologised and they said 'We can see that there's not much you could have done'," he said.

"Maybe I'll get a little bit told off but there's nothing intentional.

"They know that there's no point attacking me because it's not what I wanted."

title: Aston Martin handed worrying 'out of solutions' message by Honda during Baku misery
excerpt:
Aston Martin and Honda endured a challenging weekend in Baku, with a double DNF on Saturday.

Honda has conceded it was "out of solutions" as it endured a challenging weekend at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The Japanese manufacturer anticipated that it would be a difficult event, with the high-speed track proving to be a major obstacle for its power units.

Both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll retired from Saturday's race, marking its fourth double-DNF of the campaign.

With the long straights bringing the package's weaknesses to light, Honda admitted there was little it could do to soften the blow.

"It was a tough lesson learnt in Baku this weekend," said Honda's chief engineer Shintaro Orihara.

"We knew the long straight configuration would be a challenge for our current package.

"We have tried to minimise the time lost, but we were simply out of solutions with the tools we have available for now.

"This was a character-building weekend for everyone. I would like to thank the whole team for pushing no matter how hard the road is ahead of us."

Honda explain Alonso engine concerns

Ahead of the race weekend, Alonso and Stroll were fitted with new power unit components, ensuring they would start the race from the back of the grid.

However, after noticing a potential issue with Alonso's engine on Thursday, Honda made some more changes, though it is confident that there are no overhanging issues with the fresh engine.

"We introduced a new engine, then in FP2 we found some irregular signals on our system.

"Because it was a new engine, we decided to protect the new engine, and we did an inspection after the session, and we found the cause.

"We replaced the part and in FP3 and qualifying, we haven't seen any issue on the engine.

"So I believe the new engine is healthy. We will carry that engine for the rest of the season."

title: Liam Lawson baffled after being 'smoked' by Arvid Lindblad
excerpt:
Liam Lawson was left baffled after being "smoked" by Racing Bulls team-mate Arvid Lindblad during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Lawson was an unfortunate victim of a chain reaction sparked by an incident ahead, which saw Franco Colapinto wipe out Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris at Turn 1 following a restart on lap 36 after a crash involving Williams' Alex Albon.

As a consequence, Haas driver Esteban Ocon reacted, forcing Lindblad into the side of Lawson, who retired with severe damage to his car.

Whilst conducting an initial interview with Sky Sports F1, and explaining what unfolded, Lawson said: "We're all coming into Turn 1 on the restart, and I just got smoked from my left, put a hole in my floor as well.

"I don't really know what gap he was looking for in the middle of both of us going into Turn 1. I just don't understand it, but yeah, obviously great points for the team."

It was at that stage that Lindblad pulled Lawson away to explain the situation from his perspective.

Despite that, Lawson repeated what occurred in a separate interview with the written media, including RacingNews365.

"We're coming into Turn 1, I had a massive boost lag, and I didn't have any power, so Esteban was next to me, and I tried to give him space, and then I just got hit from my left so hard that it put a hole in the floor, and we couldn't really fight after that," said Lawson.

"I don't really know what happened, but obviously from where I'm sitting, there's not really space to go through the middle there.

"Going into Turn 1, to try and fit in between the middle of two cars like that, I don't think it's ever really going to happen.

"He came to apologise, said he locked up and he had nowhere to go. It's not ideal."

[Article continues below]

FIA stewards explain Lawson Lindblad decision

The stewards looked at the incident during the race and decided there was no case to answer, and that Lindblad was squeezed with nowhere to go.

A stewards' document read: "Following the restart, Lindblad and Lawson approached Turn 1, with Lindblad in a three-car situation.

"Ahead of them, a collision occurred involving Colapinto, Gasly and Norris. That incident, together with Colapinto locking his brakes, triggered a braking reaction among the cars immediately ahead of Lindblad.

"At the same time, Lindblad was positioned between cars on either side.

"During the corner, Lindblad made contact with Lawson.

"Having reviewed the positioning and movement of the cars involved, the stewards determined that the contact was primarily the result of the restricted space available to Lindblad and the chain reaction caused by the incident ahead, rather than any action or error for which Lindblad could be considered wholly or predominantly to blame.

"The stewards, therefore, considered this to be a typical first-corner incident following a restart, with no driver predominantly to blame."

title: Lando Norris latest online abuse victim after Franco Colapinto 'race ban' comment
excerpt:
Despite Franco Colapinto urging his fans this very week to refrain from posting online abuse towards drivers, Lando Norris has been targeted after the Azerbaijan GP.

Lando Norris has become the subject of a wave of online abuse after calling for Franco Colapinto to be handed a race ban following the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

The McLaren driver's race in Baku ended on lap 35 when Colapinto, restarting on cold tyres behind the safety car, locked up heavily into Turn 1, collecting Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly before also taking out Norris on the outside line. All three cars were eliminated on the spot, with stewards subsequently handing Colapinto a 10-second penalty he never got to serve.

Norris reacted by saying the FIA needed tougher disciplinary standards, arguing that at least a one-race ban should follow avoidable multi-car pileups caused on safety car restarts, and suggesting some drivers simply should not be in Formula 1.

Those comments have since drawn a furious response from Colapinto's fanbase on social media platform X, with numerous posts targeting Norris using explicit and homophobic language, alongside a flood of LGBTQ+ flag emojis.

"Lando Norris can suck my dick real good," read one post. "Until today Franco was the only driver who had completed all the races of the year and now because of one mistake he doesn't deserve to be in Formula 1?"

Some accounts pointed to Norris's own record, referencing his collision with Oscar Piastri at last year's Canadian Grand Prix and the wheel-banging incident with his team-mate in Singapore, both of which drew penalties or internal sanction from McLaren.

"Lando Norris can go fuck himself," another message read. "So, how many bans should he have received for Singapore and Canada just last year?"

The abuse has extended beyond X, with Argentine fans also posting hostile comments on a Norris Instagram upload from 17 September.

Colapinto's fanbase has been linked to abuse aimed at several other drivers since his F1 debut, including Yuki Tsunoda after an Imola practice incident in 2025, and Jack Doohan, who received death threats when he lost his Alpine seat to Colapinto.

Gasly and his family were also targeted following strategy tension at this year's Spanish Grand Prix.

Not everyone has piled on Norris, however. Several fans have defended the Briton, pointing out that he remains a world champion and race winner who, like every driver on the grid, is entitled to voice frustration, especially given McLaren's struggles to hand him a competitive car through his title defence.

"World champion, whether you like it or not," one fan wrote in support of Norris. "He’s angry, it’s a buildup of things and it’s completely understandable. His team hasn’t given him a decent car to defend his title since the very beginning of the season and now there’s this incident, which was COMPLETELY Franco’s fault, something he admitted himself.

"Stop giving him s***. You’re not doing anything but hurting Franco. You always do this and never learn, you make all of us look bad. Come on, Lando. One stumble doesn’t mean you’ve fallen"

Others argued the Baku incident was clearly Colapinto's own fault, something the Argentine had already admitted himself, and urged critics to stop directing anger at Norris over a result that cost him what would only have been a ninth-place finish.

"Lando has every right to complain," insisted another account. "Every single driver on the grid complains and calls things out. At the end of the day, he’s STILL a world champion and a race winner. He’s earned that."

excerpt:
When can Kimi Antonelli win the 2026 F1 drivers' championship title?

Following the 2026 Azerbaijan Grand Prix, Kimi Antonelli holds a 66-point lead over Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

No other driver is within 100 points of the Italian, who is increasingly set to become the youngest F1 world champion and shatter Sebastian Vettel's record of 23 years, 4 months, 11 days by over three years.

Antonelli, who turned 20 in August 2026, has dominated the season, but when can the Mercedes driver become the first Italian to be crowned world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953?

The article continues below.

THIS ARTICLE WILL BE UPDATED FOLLOWING EVERY GRAND PRIX UNTIL ANTONELLI WINS THE 2026 F1 WORLD DRIVERS' TITLE.

When can Kimi Antonelli win the title?

After the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, there are eight races scheduled to take place in the season, each worth 25 points.

This gives a total of 200 points remaining, which climbs to 208 once the eight points on offer in the Singapore Sprint race are added.

A scenario exists whereby Antonelli could win the title in the United States, which is laid out below.

Antonelli wins in Bahrain; Russell scores 0 points. The gap extends to 91 points.

Antonelli wins the Singapore Sprint; Russell scores 0 points. The gap extends to 99 points.

Antonelli wins in Singapore; Russell scores 0 points. The gap extends to 124 points.

Following Singapore, 150 points will remain in the season, with Antonelli potentially holding a 124-point lead.

It would mean that heading to the United States GP in Austin, Russell would be required to win every grand prix, with Antonelli not scoring another point.

If Russell failed to win in the United States under the points scenario above, Antonelli would be crowned champion regardless of what he did.

If Antonelli is exactly 125 points ahead of Russell after the Austin race, he would win the title on wins countback, as he would hold 10 grand prix victories to Russell on three, which could climb to eight over the final five races.

In terms of points ties, the number of wins is used as the first tie-breaker, and if Antonelli has won in Bahrain and Singapore, Russell cannot catch him in that metric, thus sealing Antonelli's title.

title: Isack Hadjar discovers podium fate after Azerbaijan GP investigation
excerpt:
Isack Hadjar had finished third in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix - his second podium finish of the season.

Isack Hadjar has kept his third-place podium finish at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix after a stewards' investigation.

The Frenchman, on his return to action following missing the last three grands prix with a wrist injury, finished third in Baku behind race-winner George Russell and Hadjar's team-mate, Max Verstappen.

However, post-race, the stewards summoned Hadjar over a practice start infringement before the grand prix and for failing to follow the race director's instructions on where to conduct the practice starts.

In their investigation, the stewards found that during the reconnaissance laps, Hadjar did not perform a practice start, and as per the instructions, should have crossed the white line separating pit exit from the track at the "earliest opportunity to join the normal racing line."

Hadjar remained within the pit-exit road, and passed to the right of the cars ahead before rejoining the track and, as such, had failed to follow the instructions.

However, "mitigating circumstances" were present, as Hadjar had to abort the plan to do a practice start, and the panel accepted that Hadjar was "distracted" in his failure to follow the rules.

"While the driver remains responsible for complying with the Race Director’s instructions, the Stewards considered these circumstances sufficient to mitigate the penalty. Having also considered comparable previous incidents, the Stewards therefore determine that a Warning, rather than a Driving Reprimand, is appropriate," concluded the document.

The article continues below.

Elsewhere, Carlos Sainz of Williams will keep his 10th place and first point since Monaco after being investigated for a similar offence.

Here, it was found that Sainz had been issued with an incorrect instruction by the team and followed this, leading to the breach. As such, as "lesser penalty" was appropriate.

Valtteri Bottas escaped with a 'no further action' after his late accident, crashing into the Turn 15 wall.

It was found that after climbing from the Cadillac, he stayed in the vicinity of the car, inspecting it rather than moving to a place of safety immediately.

He apologised for this and told the stewards he would immediately move to place of safety in future.

Finally, Gabriel Bortoleto received a 10-second time penalty for overtaking under yellow flags.

The Audi driver was handed the drop for passing Sergio Perez under yellow flags during the first lap after the restart.

It was found that Bortoleto was unsure if the safety car had been deployed due to conflicting information as boards showed it had been, when in reality, it had not.

Believing the yellows to be linked to the safety car deployment, and that there wasn't a dangerous situation, he overtook Perez.

For this, he received a 10-second drop, as he fell from 13th on the road to 15th, with Oscar Piastri and Perez shuffling forward one spot each.

title: Flavio Briatore threatens Alpine 'action' after costly Franco Colapinto error
excerpt:
Alpine could take matters into their own hands when it comes to Franco Colapinto.

Flavio Briatore has stated he will consider the “course of action” he will take with Franco Colapinto following his collision with team-mate Pierre Gasly during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

At a safety car restart on Saturday, Colapinto got his Turn 1 approach notably wrong and ran into the side of Gasly, who in turn made contact with Lando Norris.

All three drivers were ultimately forced to retire from the race, marking a hugely disappointing result for Alpine at a race in which it looked likely to score points.

Colapinto stated after the race that he apologised to the team and Gasly following the missed opportunity.

Briatore has now suggested that he could take action and punish Colapinto internally.

“I feel very sorry for the team and for Pierre who did a great job all weekend and my apologies also go to Lando [Norris] and McLaren for ruining their race,” he said.

“I know that Franco has taken full responsibility for it, as he should; in fact he braked far too late considering the context of the race and the safety car restart.

“It was a very poor move for a driver of his experience. I want to take time to reflect on it and consider what course of action should be taken, so we can learn from it and avoid such a situation in future.”

Colapinto concedes to being 'out of control' at restart

Prior to the incident, Gasly and Colapinto were both running inside the top 10 and looked to be on course for a double-point result.

However, its non-finish gifted an opportunity to its rivals, with Racing Bulls stretching its advantage in the fight for sixth place.

Colapinto was slapped with a 10-second time penalty for the race, but as he failed to serve it due to his DNF, it has been converted into a five-place grid drop for Sepang.

Explaining what he experienced behind the wheel, Colapinto said: “I locked up with cold tyres, cold brakes, and was out of control.

“I know the team has done a good job all weekend with the performance of the car.

“I am really sorry for what happened as we were in a good position to score double points.”

title: Franco Colapinto hit with further penalty after Azerbaijan calamity
excerpt:
Franco Colapinto was initially handed a 10-second time penalty by the stewards for the accident in which he eliminated three cars, including himself.

Franco Colapinto has been handed a five-place grid penalty for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but avoided penalty points for his calamity in Azerbaijan.

On the safety car restart in Baku, Colapinto locked up on the inside, and being "out of control" he collided with team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris, forcing both into immediate retirement as he crawled back to the pits, costing Alpine a huge haul of points.

The Argentine then retired himself and was handed a 10-second penalty for causing a collision - the standard penalty - but was unable to serve it as he had already retired.

In line with normal practice, this 10-second penalty has now been converted into a grid drop for Colapinto's next event.

This will be the Bahrain GP next weekend, which is being held in Malaysia at Sepang. He will drop five places from where he qualifies.

Elsewhere, Colapinto avoided any more points on his superlicence, meaning his rolling tally for the 12-month period stays at four, with 12 required to trigger a one-race ban.

The article continues below.

Stewards decision in full

Following the restart, COL approached GAS from behind into Turn 1.

COL braked too late and entered the corner on the inside at a speed which did not allow him to make the corner in a controlled manner. He overshot the corner and made contact with the left-hand side of GAS, who then hit NOR and both cars retired.

The Stewards considered that COL was wholly or predominantly to blame for the collision.

Although the incident occurred at the first corner following the restart, there was no contribution from another driver which would justify applying the first-lap / first- corner more linient approach.

The standard penalty for causing a collision is a 10-second time penalty. As COL had retired from the Race and was therefore unable to serve the time penalty, the Stewards converted the penalty to a drop of 5 grid positions at the next Race in which the driver participates in accordance which Article B1.9.6.(e) of the FIA FIA 2026 F1 Regulations.

title: Ranked: Top 10 closest F1 finishes after George Russell-Max Verstappen thriller
excerpt:
George Russell narrowly beat Max Verstappen in a thrilling finale to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix - by just 0.196s.

Russell was on course for a grand chelem, but had to fend off Verstappen in the closing stages as he was hunted by the Dutchman in the closing laps after a safety car restart.

The Mercedes driver did hold off Verstappen to record that grand chelem, and in the process, recorded the 10th closest green-flag finish in all 1,164 world championship grands prix to date, including Azerbaijan 2026.

The closest ever finish was at pre-chicane Monza in 1971 when Peter Gethin beat Ronnie Peterson by 0.010s, although the times were measured to hundredths of a second, whereas the 0.011s between Rubens Barrichello and Michael Schumacher at the 2002 United States GP was to thousandths.

One of the most famous wins in F1 history is also in the top 10, as Giancarlo Baghetti won the 1961 French GP by 0.100s from Dan Gurney.

Giuseppe Farina's victory in the very first world championship grand prix aside, Baghetti's win, his only in a world championship grand prix, is the only occasion where a driver has won on his debut.

title: Lando Norris scathingly criticises Franco Colapinto: 'Some drivers shouldn't be in F1'
excerpt:
Lando Norris has taken aim at Franco Colapinto after the Alpine driver wiped him — and Pierre Gasly — out of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Lando Norris has hit out at Franco Colapinto after the Alpine driver forced him and Pierre Gasly into retirement at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

At the first safety car restart, Colapinto locked up and came hurtling up the inside of the first corner, slamming into his team-mate and Norris, with all three unable to continue.

The McLaren driver was already enduring a testing afternoon at the Baku City Circuit. The woeful straight-line speed of his MCL40 left him powerless to defend positions, before a mistake at Turn 1 saw him tumble further down the order and into a fight with the Alpines at the tail end of the points.

"I was just slow — struggling a lot in the straights; you saw how quickly everyone came past me," Norris said after the race.

"An impossible race out there for me from that side and straight-line speed, so hopefully we get that fixed for next time."

Norris' brutal criticism of Colapinto

The reigning F1 drivers' champion did not hold back in his criticism of Colapinto, who has recently extended his contract with Alpine for the 2027 season.

Norris gave a forthright appraisal of his counterpart, arguing he is not worthy of his place on the grid and that he is deserving of a one-race ban for the incident, à la Romain Grosjean in 2012.

"But otherwise, I still made the mistake, and at the end of the day, I just got taken out," the 13-time grand prix winner added.

"So just some drivers that shouldn't be in Formula 1, to be honest."

title: Fred Vasseur responds to Christian Horner Ferrari rumours
excerpt:
Fred Vasseur has responded to rumours that Christian Horner could replace him as Ferrari F1 team principal.

Horner is currently promoting his upcoming book as he seeks a return to grand prix racing, where he has made clear that he would not settle for being a mere team principal and was seeking an ownership stake in a team after his exit from Red Bull in 2025.

However, speaking to The Times, Horner declared: "I’ve been a hired hand. I did 21 years sitting on the pit wall. I don’t need to go back to that. At this stage in my life, there’s only one team for which I would accept non-participation in ownership.

"Would I consider Ferrari? I mean, Ferrari is the biggest brand in Formula 1. It’s the dream. And arguably it’s the sleeping giant of Formula 1."

Horner had been linked with Ferrari previously when he was at Red Bull, but the move did not materalise. However, given Ferrari's faltered title challenge in 2026, Italian media have begun to be critical once again of Vasseur, who assumed control of the team in 2023.

RacingNews365 understands that a plan is provisionally being drawn up for how Ferrari could manage Vasseur's exit at the end of the season, if the Frenchman decided to step down.

Over the course of the Azerbaijan GP weekend, rumours in the paddock intensified around the possibility of Vasseur's exit at the end of the year, which grew in strength.

Reacting to the rumours for the first time publicly, Vasseur was not impressed with the line of questioning, nor did he shut down the links to Horner completely.

"We are not working in perfect serenity, as it is the question for me first and for everybody in the team, for the media; 50% of the questions are about this, and that is a bit of a frustrating situation," Vasseur told the media, including RacingNews365, after Ferrari finished fourth and sixth, behind Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in Azerbaijan.

"We are fighting for the championship, and at the end of the day, we are speaking a lot about this and for the guys in the garage, it is not the best discussion we can have, but it is what it is.

"It is not in my hands, and Horner is looking for a job, everybody knows, everywhere, but what can I do?

"Just try to do my best to move the team, to raise them and to be better than today, and then to spend time with you [the media], where each interview, it will be 25 times a day, we are coming back on this.

"What can I do? What can I say?"

When asked if he was fully committed, Vasseur replied: "Sure, this sport is my life, it is my business, and I try to do my best. I'm here to do my job, and I have the best job in the world, and we still have seven races to go."

Vasseur was then asked if he would like to work with Horner in the future, Vasseur quipped: 'You have to ask my assistant.'

title: Franco Colapinto issues 'out of control' apology after wiping out Pierre Gasly and Lando Norris
excerpt:
Franco Colapinto has issued an apology to Alpine F1 team-mate Pierre Gasly and McLaren's Lando Norris for eliminating them from the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

On a safety car restart following Alex Albon's crash, with both Alpines in the points, Colapinto was on the inside of Turn 1, but locked up heavily and was "out of control" as the field headed to the pinch-point of the apex.

As the drivers ahead turned in, Colapinto's team-mate Gasly and the reigning champion Norris were both collected by the Argentine, who crawled back to the pits to retire.

Post-race, Norris called for a one-race ban for drivers who commit such actions, with Colapinto being handed a 10s penalty by the stewards, which is likely to be converted to a grid penalty for Bahrain as he could not serve it.

Reflecting, Colapinto described the events which had taken place - and how he ended "out of control."

"It is a big mistake. I locked up completely the tyres and the brakes and was out of control completely," Colapinto told media, including RacingNews365.

"There is not a lot more to say than to say sorry to the team and to Pierre, of course. The team has been working really hard to score points, and I threw it away with a big mistake, so I am sad for the team.

"Of course it is more disappointing to take out your team-mate; that is the biggest part of it. If I make a mistake and it only affects me, it is okay to learn, but when it affects the other car as well, it is important.

"It is a big mistake, and I take full responsibility for it, and it is something to learn and take on the chin, and hopefully we'll keep working.

"I spoke with Pierre; he came back, and of course, he is very upset."

Turning to Norris's demand for a race ban for the Alpine driver, Colapinto again apologised.

"I am sorry to Lando for doing that, as I also took him out, not just Pierre," he said.

"It was just a mistake, and I was out of control; I couldn't do a lot. I locked up as soon as I touched the brakes."
